clue.text: Lower class compartments with first-class return taking drunken pals back

indicators.note: drunken means reeling and jumbled, so the letters of pals are rearranged
back says the pair of pieces before it are each read in the opposite direction

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI
RET is a common abbreviation for return

explanation.surface: A rail journey where tipsy friends are taken back in cheap carriages with a first-class return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is a cow (one that lows), so the 'lower class' is cattle. 'drunken' turns PALS into PSAL; 'back' turns AI and RET into IA and TER, giving TERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The psalterium is the third stomach chamber of cattle and other ruminants, so its plural names compartments in the bodies of the mooing class.

clue.text: Prince absent from Scotland with tribal convention

parts.note: AWA is the Scots form of away, meaning absent

explanation.surface: A royal skips a Scottish visit in favour of a tribal gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawaw is an old spelling of powwow, a council or meeting of Native American tribes.

clue.text: Ascertain, as it were, right? You bet your life!

parts.note: to assure is roughly to make sure, which is what ascertaining amounts to

explanation.surface: Someone checks a fact and is told emphatically that it is so.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as an emphatic 'certainly', but literally a life policy is a bet on your life taken by an insurer.
explanation.definitionFit: A life assurance company in effect wagers on how long you will live, so it is the party you bet your life with.

clue.text: Upstate French gallery builder!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is written from the bottom upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: ETAT is the French word for state; the matching run of letters that also sits inside Upstate is a coincidence of the split

explanation.surface: A French art patron from upstate New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstate' looks like one word, but it splits into 'Up', the reversal signal, and 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, founded and paid for the Tate Gallery in London.

clue.text: Knight managed to switch position

indicators.note: switching the two pieces puts the knight after the verb rather than before it

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: A knight on a chessboard changes square.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank is a standing or position in a hierarchy, as in a person's rank in society.

clue.text: Energy departing old has-beens wrecked by such hairy beauties

indicators.note: wrecked means ruined and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Faded celebrities, worn out and wrecked, contrast with glamorous fair-haired women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departing' says the E (energy) leaves OLD HASBEENS before 'wrecked' rearranges what remains, OLDHASBNS plus the second E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blondes are women whose hair is a pale, greyish fair colour, so they are beauties described by their hair.

clue.text: 10s 22's take on 18 12, Bassenthwaite, Tbilisi and Volta with little revision

indicators.note: a revision reworks text, so these place names have their letters reordered

parts.note: a little form of with is its abbreviation W

explanation.surface: A poet's view of a historic upheaval set against a list of a Lakeland lake, a Georgian capital and an African river.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is WORD and 22 WORTH, so '10s 22's' is Wordsworth; 18 12 is THE FRENCH REVOLUTION. The line comes from his poem on it. The fodder here includes 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous line from Wordsworth's The Prelude expresses his youthful elation at the outbreak of the revolution in France.

clue.text: Where Bragg's maid was, say, married and bereft without measure outside

indicators.note: outside says the shortened word goes around the other pieces
without means the measure is taken out of bereft

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot, a measure
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A girl from a novel is married and left bereaved.
explanation.walkthrough: Melvyn Bragg wrote The Maid of Buttermere, about a girl from that Lake District village.
explanation.definitionFit: Bragg's novel tells of Mary Robinson, the beauty of an inn in this Cumbrian lake village.

clue.text: The Turk's Head for such hostelries, say? Is mater upset?

definitions.text: The Turk's Head for such hostelries, say?

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub called The Turk's Head and a worried mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Imarets are Turkish hospices or inns for travellers, and a pub named after a Turk would suit them.

clue.text: Anvil Chorus from this composer?

parts.note: the hammering song of Verdi's blacksmiths, imagined as by a metalworker who makes music

explanation.definitionFit: A writer of songs, a tunesmith, punningly a blacksmith of melodies.

clue.text: See 6
Message given by 2

definitions.meaning: a ... is a brief message or piece of news, as in sending ...
2 down is the assurer, and an assurer gives a promise

explanation.definitionFit: Word means a message, and one's word is the promise an assurer gives.

clue.text: Shed no light thus? That's stupid!

definitions.meaning: with no hint or pointer at all, nothing would be illuminated
dim or witless, describing a foolish person

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a clue sheds no light on the matter, and the colloquial adjective also means dim-witted.

clue.text: See 18
One's exported, exploited and leaves with ruination

indicators.note: ruination wrecks the letters of the phrase before it, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sent abroad and exploited departs in ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A white slave is a woman trafficked abroad for forced prostitution, so exported and exploited.

clue.text: She emerged from the Ottoman's clutches

definitions.text: She emerged from the Ottoman's clutches

parts.words: She emerged from the Ottoman's clutches
parts.note: read as a female bird hatched from a clutch of eggs, with the Ottoman standing for the country of that name

explanation.definitionFit: The female of the farmyard gobbler, which hatches from a clutch of eggs.

clue.text: See 6 across
Grandma's aiming to entrap a black warrior

indicators.note: entrapping means holding something inside, so the answer is caught within these words

explanation.surface: A grandmother sets out to catch a warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are an East African people famed as warriors and herders.

clue.text: Party at which Ecstasy proscription goes around and round

indicators.note: goes around says the ban encloses the drug's letter

parts.note: a ban is a proscription or prohibition
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A rave where a ban on Ecstasy keeps circulating.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Pique at religious publication

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at a religious pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique interest is to arouse or draw it, as attracting does.

clue.text: El

parts.note: the French word for 'the' is le; give it a ..., turning it round, and these two letters result

explanation.definitionFit: Le is French for the, and the clue word is that article turned round, a revolution of it.

clue.text: Impotent potentate?

definitions.meaning: powerless, split as a phrase meaning incapable
a ruler or grandee, a person of importance

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word means unable, while as a noun it is a person of distinction like a ruler.

clue.text: Old German game, it's tricky for a Robin Hood

parts.note: alt is the German word for old
RU stands for rugby union, a game

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient German pastime proves tricky for an outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood robbed the rich to give to the poor, making him a type of selfless giver.

clue.text: "Stuff it!" — a public school saying

indicators.note: saying means spoken, so the school's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Stowe is a public school in Buckinghamshire, England

explanation.surface: A rude retort heard at a posh boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: STOWE is an English fee-paying boarding school; its name sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to stuff or pack it away.

clue.text: Couturier taken at face value

definitions.meaning: Charles Frederick ..., the English-born fashion designer in Paris
value or what something is reckoned to be ...

explanation.definitionFit: Charles Worth founded Parisian haute couture, and the word also means value.

clue.text: Admiral executed below yardarm, naval gunners taking off caps

indicators.note: caps are the tops, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: An admiral put to death beneath the yardarm by naval gunners firing.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral John Byng was shot by firing squad on his own quarterdeck in 1757.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral John Byng was executed by the Royal Navy for failing to relieve Minorca.

clue.text: Have to, when defining frenzy in elephants

definitions.meaning: the state of aggressive frenzy in a male elephant

explanation.definitionFit: Must is a verb of obligation and also the frenzied state of bull elephants in season.

clue.text: Illusory quantity in thoughts of summer!

definitions.meaning: a summer is one who sums, and the figure exists in their mind

explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, a multiple of the square root of minus one, and literally a figure imagined by one who adds.

clue.text: John Peel cancelling training with heavyweight

indicators.note: cancelling removes the training letters from peel

parts.note: PE is physical education, or training
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A radio DJ gives up the gym for heavy lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a famous BBC radio DJ; the definition is the singer Elton John.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is the singer whose surname here is the clue word John.

clue.text: Destroy the nameless thing that is a significant anniversary

indicators.note: destroying breaks up the letters, so they are rearranged
nameless removes the N, abbreviation for name, from thing

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A command to destroy an unnamed monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightieth anniversary or birthday is a notable milestone.
